why: If every position carries a similar slip risk, the shorter finished sample in a tie has fewer chances to derail, so the shortest-sample tie-break clearly beats a random pick (about 12 of 36).
The vote averages out independent slips (446 with the default tie rule), and sending ties to the shortest finished sample, which has the fewest slip chances, adds a few more problems.
RL's tail is small, so its votes rarely tie and its slips are rare; the shortest-sample tie-break leaves it at or just above its 474 vote.
Sending ties to the longest sample picks the answer with the most positions exposed to slips, so it falls a few problems below the shortest-sample rule.
